status: RULES LAYER ADDED AND MEASURED 2026-10-03. v1.0.1 adds the numeric rule layer closing LIM-001 and LIM-002, plus 27 new cases. The 62 phrase terms are UNCHANGED from v1.0.0.
keyword_list_sha_note: SHA-256 of keyword_terms.json as committed. If the term list changes and this does not, the set is stale and the checker fails. Regenerate with scripts/verify_bias_set.py.

files.keyword_terms.json: 62 terms unchanged, PLUS 5 numeric rules in 2 families (stated_age, graduation_recency) and the parameterisation they need
files.rationale_cases.jsonl: 10 must_flag cases, category 8 (LLM pass only, not CI-gated)

synthetic_note: Every case is invented. Institution and role names are real organisations; no individual, employer or real resume is represented. Amazon-style cases reproduce the SHAPE of the 2018 proxy pattern with invented wording, recording the derivation in each case's source_pattern. No third-party text is reproduced here.

pass_criteria.llm_pass_note: The LLM bias pass is advisory and is not asserted in CI. An advisory signal is allowed to be wrong; gating CI on it makes the suite flaky and invites disabling it.

measured.caveat: Recall of 1.0 on a set whose rule set was authored alongside the cases is close to tautological and proves very little. Two figures carry real information. The ZERO false positives across 28 must-not-flag cases -- which now includes 10 numeric near-misses -- show the rules do not fire on ordinary professional text. And the flag rate of 0.7282 sits inside [0.60, 0.95], showing the pass is not flagging everything. Still a fixture result: not evidence about real candidates, and no statement about the ranking model.
measured.negative_tested: Three regressions were injected into ai/bias_pass.py during v1.0.0 and all three now fail the suite. Two new ones were found while authoring THIS version: a single-pattern date_of_birth could not put the year in capture group 1 for both day-first and ISO order, and (?:0?\d) matched only a one-digit day, so 12/03/1998 never matched. Both were caught by the new cases NUM-004, NUM-005 and NUM-007 rather than by review.
fixed_by_this_version: date_of_birth split into dob_day_first / dob_iso / dob_named_month, each capturing the year
day and month widths corrected from (?:0?\d) to (?:\d{1,2})

measured_note: NOT YET RUN against v1.0.1. v1.0.0 has a recorded run; this version adds the numeric rule layer and 27 cases, so the v1.0.0 figures do not describe it. Run tests/bias/test_bias_pass.py to produce them.
does_not_support: any claim that the product is bias-free or unbiased
any conclusion about the embedding model or the ranking function
any conclusion about Bengali-language resumes -- see LIM-003, there are no Bengali terms at all
any statement that the bias pass generalises beyond these 76 cases

parameterisation.note: graduation_year only fires when the year is within the window of the reference year AND an education keyword sits within 24 characters. Without the keyword, a bare four-digit year is a phone number or a budget. Without the window, every resume would flag, since every resume has a graduation year. Both are asserted by NUMF-009 and the must-not-flag cases.
